_comment: The clinical chips — the headline. Each is chosen so the Auto routing badge visibly changes (RFC 0076 § The routing showcase). Token counts map onto RFC 0044's v1 policy: <=2 -> hybrid_text, >=8 -> semantic, else fused. The 'note' is shown in the Routing inspector to teach the router.

examples.note: drug + dose, 2 tokens -> hybrid_text: exact lexical, typo-tolerant. ANN would add noise on an identifier this short; BM25+fuzzy is the right tool. Never paid for an embedding.
an abbreviation, 1 token -> hybrid_text. A single clinical identifier is exactly where the keyword/fuzzy route wins and the semantic route flounders.
1 token -> hybrid_text; 'afib'/'AF'/'atrial fibrillation' surface through the fuzzy + FTS legs without an embedding.
misspelled, 1 token -> hybrid_text; the fuzzy legs (RFC 0057) still find aspirin notes through the typo — the all-typo query that semantic-only would blank.

examples.text: chest pain radiating to left arm
examples.note: a clinical phrase, 5 tokens -> fused: BM25 catches 'chest pain'/'arm', the semantic leg pulls the cardiac picture close, merged by RRF.
5 tokens -> fused: lexical leg on the words, semantic leg on the symptom — neither alone is as good as both.

examples.text: elderly woman with progressive dyspnea and bilateral lower-extremity edema
examples.note: a clinical picture in prose, 9 tokens -> semantic: ANN over the Arctic embedding, no exact words needed. Returns the heart-failure presentations even when they never say 'dyspnea'.

examples.text: recurrent pneumonia in a young adult with sinus infections
examples.note: 9 tokens -> semantic: the constellation, not the keywords, is the query. Clusters immunodeficiency presentations a keyword search would miss.
